What is the mechanistic classification of this reaction (the Dakin reaction), and what is the key migration step?
options: A) It proceeds via nucleophilic addition of hydroperoxide anion ($^-\text{OOH}$) to the carbonyl group, followed by a Baeyer-Villiger type 1,2-migration of the electron-rich ortho-hydroxyphenyl ring to the peroxy oxygen with simultaneous departure of hydroxide ion, yielding an ester intermediate that hydrolyzes to catechol
B) It proceeds via electrophilic aromatic substitution by singlet oxygen at the ortho position followed by decarbonylation
C) It proceeds via radical homolysis of hydrogen peroxide generating hydroxyl radicals that displace the formyl group directly
D) It proceeds via Cannizzaro-type disproportionation where salicylaldehyde oxidizes to salicylic acid followed by thermal decarboxylation
questions.explanation: Step 1: The Dakin reaction is the oxidation of ortho- or para-hydroxybenzaldehydes or acetophenones to benzenediols using alkaline hydrogen peroxide. Step 2: In alkaline medium, $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ is deprotonated to the hydroperoxide anion ($^-\text{OOH}$), which acts as a powerful $\alpha$-effect nucleophile and attacks the carbonyl carbon of the formyl group to form a tetrahedral adduct: $\text{Ar}-\text{CH}(\text{O}^-)-\text{O}-\text{OH}$. Step 3: In the key rate-determining rearrangement step, the electron-rich phenoxide ring migrates from the tetrahedral carbon to the adjacent peroxy oxygen atom with simultaneous cleavage of the weak peroxy $\text{O}-\text{O}$ bond and expulsion of hydroxide ion ($\text{OH}^-$). The migration is strongly accelerated by the electron-donating ortho-phenoxide group ($+M$ effect). Step 4: This migration forms a formate ester of the diol, $\text{Ar}-\text{O}-\text{CHO}$, which rapidly undergoes base-catalyzed hydrolysis to yield catechol (benzene-1,2-diol) and sodium formate. Therefore, applying mechanistic analysis confirms that statement A is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: When diols are heated in the presence of concentrated sulfuric acid or phosphoric acid, they undergo dehydration to form cyclic ethers or unsaturated compounds depending on chain length and ring stability. Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding these acid-catalyzed dehydration processes?
options: A) Heating ethane-1,2-diol (ethylene glycol) with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ at $140^\circ\text{C}$ leads to intermolecular dehydration yielding the six-membered cyclic diether 1,4-dioxane
B) Heating propane-1,3-diol with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ undergoes rapid intramolecular cyclization to produce oxetane as the predominant product in greater than $90\%$ yield

C) Heating butane-1,4-diol with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ or $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ at $100^\circ\text{C}$ undergoes facile intramolecular $S_N2$ cyclization to produce tetrahydrofuran (oxolane) in near-quantitative yield
D) Heating pentane-1,5-diol with acid results exclusively in intermolecular polymerization because seven-membered ring formation is kinetically forbidden
questions.explanation: Step 1: Ethane-1,2-diol undergoes bimolecular condensation: protonation of one hydroxyl followed by nucleophilic attack of a second glycol molecule yields diethylene glycol, which upon subsequent intramolecular acid-catalyzed cyclization forms the six-membered, strain-free ring 1,4-dioxane. Hence statement A is correct. Step 2: Statement B is false because oxetane is a four-membered ring possessing high angle strain ($\sim 106\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$). Intramolecular cyclization of propane-1,3-diol is kinetically and thermodynamically unfavored; instead, intermolecular oligomerization and dehydration to allyl alcohol predominate. Step 3: Butane-1,4-diol readily cyclizes: protonation of one $-\text{OH}$ group is followed by intramolecular nucleophilic attack by the remaining hydroxyl group to form a stable, strain-free five-membered cyclic ether (tetrahydrofuran, THF) with expulsion of water in nearly quantitative yield. Hence statement C is correct. Step 4: Statement D is false because pentane-1,5-diol cyclizes to form tetrahydropyran (oxane), which is a six-membered ring (not seven-membered) and forms in high yield. Therefore, applying ring-strain thermodynamics confirms that options A and C are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the base-catalyzed nucleophilic ring opening of enantiopure $(2R,3R)$-2,3-dimethyloxirane by sodium methoxide in methanol ($\text{NaOCH}_3/\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$). Which of the following statements correctly identifies the stereochemical configuration and optical activity of the product formed?
options: A) Attack at $\text{C}-2$ gives $(2R,3R)$-3-methoxybutan-2-ol, which is optically active, while attack at $\text{C}-3$ gives an identical enantiomer

B) Nucleophilic attack by methoxide occurs with complete inversion of configuration ($S_N2$) at the attacked carbon while leaving the unattacked carbon configuration unchanged; attack at $\text{C}-2$ yields $(2S,3R)$-3-methoxybutan-2-ol, and attack at $\text{C}-3$ yields $(2R,3S)$-3-methoxybutan-2-ol, forming an equimolar, optically inactive racemic mixture
C) The reaction proceeds with retention of configuration at both stereocenters via an $S_N i$ mechanism, yielding a meso compound
D) The epoxide ring opens via a planar carbocation intermediate ($S_N1$), yielding exclusively $(2R,3R)$-3-methoxybutan-2-ol
questions.explanation: Step 1: $(2R,3R)$-2,3-dimethyloxirane possesses $C_2$ rotational symmetry. Both epoxide carbons ($\text{C}-2$ and $\text{C}-3$) are identical in chemical reactivity and steric hindrance. Step 2: Under basic conditions, the strong nucleophile $\text{CH}_3\text{O}^-$ attacks directly via an $S_N2$ backside displacement at either $\text{C}-2$ or $\text{C}-3$. Step 3: If attack occurs at $\text{C}-2$, backside inversion changes the configuration from $(R)$ to $(S)$, while the stereocenter at $\text{C}-3$ is untouched and remains $(R)$. The product is $(2S,3R)$-3-methoxybutan-2-ol. Step 4: Because of symmetry, attack at $\text{C}-3$ occurs with equal probability ($50\%$), inverting $\text{C}-3$ from $(R)$ to $(S)$ while keeping $\text{C}-2$ as $(R)$, yielding $(2R,3S)$-3-methoxybutan-2-ol. Step 5: The two enantiomeric products $(2S,3R)$ and $(2R,3S)$ are formed in exactly a $1:1$ ratio, resulting in an optically inactive racemic mixture. Distractor A ignores the enantiomeric relationship, C proposes an $S_N i$ mechanism impossible under basic conditions, and D assumes carbocation formation without acid catalysis. Therefore, applying stereochemical inversion rules confirms that option B is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Phenols exhibit diverse reactivity toward electrophilic and oxidative reagents. Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding azo coupling, persulfate oxidation, and aminoxyl radical oxidation of phenol?
options: A) Phenol couples with benzenediazonium chloride in weakly alkaline solution ($\text{pH } 9-10$) to yield 4-hydroxyazobenzene as an orange azo dye, because phenoxide is the active nucleophilic species

B) Oxidation of phenol with potassium nitrosodisulfonate (Fremy's salt, $(\text{KSO}_3)_2\text{NO}^\bullet$) in aqueous acetone proceeds via a radical mechanism to yield 1,4-benzoquinone in high yield
C) In the azo coupling of phenol, if the reaction mixture is maintained at strongly acidic $\text{pH } < 2$, the coupling rate increases dramatically due to protonation of the diazonium ion
D) In the Elbs persulfate oxidation, monohydric phenols are converted into dihydric phenols (principally quinols) by reaction with alkaline potassium persulfate ($\text{K}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_8$)
questions.explanation: Step 1: In azo coupling of phenol, the weakly electrophilic diazonium cation ($\text{Ph}-\text{N}_2^+$) requires a strongly activated aromatic ring. In alkaline medium ($\text{pH } 9-10$), phenol is converted to the phenoxide anion ($\text{Ph}-\text{O}^-$), whose intense $+M$ resonance activation facilitates rapid electrophilic coupling at the para position to give 4-hydroxyazobenzene (orange dye). Hence statement A is correct. Step 2: At low $\text{pH} < 2$, phenol exists entirely in the unionized, much less reactive neutral form, and the coupling rate drops to virtually zero. Diazonium salts are already fully formed in acid and do not become more reactive by further protonation. Hence statement C is false. Step 3: Fremy's salt (potassium nitrosodisulfonate, a stable aminoxyl free radical) selectively oxidizes phenols having an open para position via phenoxy radical intermediates to 1,4-benzoquinone in excellent yield under mild conditions. Hence statement B is correct. Step 4: Elbs persulfate oxidation uses $\text{K}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_8$ in alkaline aqueous solution to introduce an $-\text{OH}$ group into the para position of phenols, producing quinols (hydroquinones). Hence statement D is correct. Therefore, applying reaction kinetics and mechanisms shows that options A, B, and D are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: When $(1R,2S)$-1-amino-1,2-diphenylpropan-2-ol is treated with nitrous acid ($\text{HNO}_2$) at $0^\circ\text{C}$, it undergoes a stereospecific semipinacol rearrangement with loss of nitrogen gas ($\text{N}_2$). What is the stereoelectronic requirement that governs which group migrates from $\text{C}-2$ to $\text{C}-1$, and what is the major ketone product?
options: A) Migrating group is always the one with higher intrinsic migratory aptitude ($p\text{-anisyl} > \text{phenyl} > \text{alkyl}$), regardless of conformational alignment; product is 1,2-diphenylpropan-1-one
B) Hydride migrates exclusively via a planar four-membered transition state to form 1,2-diphenylpropan-2-one

C) The migrating group must be aligned anti-periplanar (dihedral angle $\approx 180^\circ$) to the departing diazonium leaving group ($-\text{N}_2^+$) in the lowest-energy ground-state conformation, governing migration stereoelectronically
D) Diazotization forms a free carbocation at $\text{C}-1$ that completely equilibrates before migration occurs, losing all stereochemical information
questions.explanation: Step 1: Treatment of a $\beta$-amino alcohol with nitrous acid ($\text{HNO}_2$) converts the primary amino group into an exceptionally good leaving group, the diazonium ion ($-\text{N}_2^+$). Step 2: Unlike the classical pinacol rearrangement where a carbocation is formed and migratory aptitude dictates the shifting group, the departure of molecular nitrogen in semipinacol deamination is concerted with the 1,2-migration. Step 3: The stereoelectronic requirement of this concerted displacement demands that the $\sigma$-bonding orbital of the migrating group be anti-periplanar (dihedral angle $\approx 180^\circ$) to the $\sigma^*$ antibonding orbital of the $\text{C}-\text{N}_2^+$ bond. Step 4: The ground-state conformation that places the leaving group and migrating group anti-periplanar dictates which group shifts, overriding conventional migratory aptitudes. Thus, applying orbital symmetry and stereoelectronic control confirms that statement C is correct. Distractor A ignores stereoelectronics, B assumes an impossible planar transition state, and D falsely asserts a long-lived free carbocation.

questions.questionText:
Consider the following synthetic sequence starting from 1,2-dimethoxybenzene (veratrole):
Step 1: Veratrole is treated with 1.0 equivalent of boron tribromide ($\text{BBr}_3$) in dichloromethane at $-78^\circ\text{C}$ followed by aqueous workup to yield compound $A$.
Step 2: Compound $A$ is treated with allyl bromide in the presence of anhydrous potassium carbonate ($\text{K}_2\text{CO}_3$) in acetone to yield compound $B$.
Step 3: Compound $B$ is heated to $200^\circ\text{C}$ in $N,N$-diethylaniline to undergo a Claisen rearrangement, affording compound $C$.
Step 4: Compound $C$ is treated with a catalytic amount of concentrated sulfuric acid or $\text{Hg(OAc)}_2$ followed by reductive workup to undergo intramolecular cyclization, forming compound $D$.
Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding this reaction sequence?
options: A) In Step 1, $\text{BBr}_3$ selectively cleaves only one of the methyl ether groups via Lewis acid coordination and nucleophilic attack by $\text{Br}^-$, cleanly yielding 2-methoxyphenol (guaiacol) as compound $A$
B) In Step 2, Williamson etherification of guaiacol with allyl bromide occurs chemoselectively at the free phenolic hydroxyl group to afford 1-(allyloxy)-2-methoxybenzene as compound $B$
C) In Step 3, the thermal Claisen rearrangement of compound $B$ proceeds via a [3,3]-sigmatropic shift to the unoccupied ortho position, yielding 2-allyl-6-methoxyphenol as compound $C$

D) In Step 4, acid-catalyzed cyclization of compound $C$ proceeds via electrophilic addition of $\text{H}^+$ to the allyl double bond followed by intramolecular capture of the resulting carbocation by the phenolic $-\text{OH}$ group according to Markovnikov's rule, yielding 7-methoxy-2-methyl-2,3-dihydrobenzofuran as compound $D$
questions.explanation: Step 1: Boron tribromide ($\text{BBr}_3$) is a premier reagent for the mild, selective deprotection of aryl methyl ethers. Using 1.0 equivalent at low temperature ($-78^\circ\text{C}$) selectively mono-demethylates veratrole (1,2-dimethoxybenzene) to 2-methoxyphenol (guaiacol, $A$). Hence statement A is correct. Step 2: In the presence of $\text{K}_2\text{CO}_3$, guaiacol is deprotonated to its phenoxide, which undergoes facile $S_N2$ allylation with allyl bromide to yield allyl 2-methoxyphenyl ether ($B$). Hence statement B is correct. Step 3: Thermal activation of $B$ at $200^\circ\text{C}$ triggers an aromatic [3,3]-sigmatropic Claisen rearrangement. The allyl group migrates cleanly to the vacant ortho position relative to the allyloxy group, followed by tautomerization to yield 2-allyl-6-methoxyphenol ($C$). Hence statement C is correct. Step 4: In Step 4, treatment of 2-allyl-6-methoxyphenol ($C$) with acid protonates the terminal double bond to give a secondary carbocation at $\text{C}-2'$: $\text{Ar}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}^+-\text{CH}_3$. Intramolecular nucleophilic capture by the adjacent phenolic oxygen forms a stable five-membered dihydrofuran ring (Markovnikov addition), yielding 7-methoxy-2-methyl-2,3-dihydrobenzofuran ($D$). Therefore, applying mechanistic analysis shows that all statements A, B, C, and D are correct.
